questions.question: Which kinematic regime isolates the ballistic contribution to drag in this analysis?

options.A: ql≫1 and ωτ≫1, with disturbance scales shorter than the mean free path and scattering time
options.B: ql≪1 and ωτ≪1, with diffusion dominating at long scales
options.C: qR≪1 and ω/Ω≫1, independent of mean free path
options.D: ql≫1 and ωτ≪1, with static disorder controlling response

questions.rationale: The paper characterizes ballistic response by nonlocal wavevectors and frequencies high relative to the scattering rate.
questions.evidence_quote: scales are smaller than the mean free path l of electrons (ql ≫ 1)

questions.question: Why do the authors reject earlier asymptotic conductivity formulas for their calculation away from half filling?

options.A: Those formulas fail to approach Beff→0 smoothly at finite q
options.B: They are restricted to diffusive transport with ql≪1
options.C: They assume noninteracting electrons rather than composite fermions
options.D: They omit the Hall component of the conductivity tensor

questions.rationale: The desired result must remain smooth as the effective field tends to zero at finite wavevector.
questions.evidence_quote: they do not provide a smooth passage to the Beff → 0 limit at finite q

questions.question: What route is used to derive the suitable composite-fermion conductivity approximation?

options.A: Solve the Boltzmann transport equation for the CF distribution and expand the resulting conductivity
options.B: Use a Kubo formula with exact diagonalization of two coupled Landau levels
options.C: Fit measured drag curves and infer conductivity from a Drude model
options.D: Apply a hydrodynamic constitutive relation to the bilayer polarization matrix

questions.rationale: They start from the standard Boltzmann solution and transform it to obtain conductivity components.
questions.evidence_quote: we start from the standard solution of the Boltzmann transport equation

options.A: Powers of (qR)⁻¹, where R=vF/Ω is the CF cyclotron radius

options.C: Powers of ωτ, with R the mean free path
options.D: Powers of (qd)⁻¹, where d is the CF orbit diameter

questions.rationale: The expansion is organized in inverse qR using the defined cyclotron radius.

questions.question: What scaling estimate for δ=ω/(qvF) supports the low-temperature approximation?

options.A: δ∼(T/μ)(T0/T)^(1/3), small at low T when T0 is room-temperature scale
options.B: δ∼(μ/T)(T/T0)^(1/3), small only when T exceeds T0
options.D: δ∼(T/μ)(T/T0)^(1/3), which diverges as T decreases

questions.rationale: The dominant q and ω scales yield the stated estimate, which is small at about 1 K for room-temperature-scale T0.

questions.question: How does the ν=1/2 CF compressibility compare with the zero-field noninteracting density of states N?

options.A: It is 3m*/(8πℏ²), versus N=m*/(2πℏ²), reflecting Chern–Simons interactions
options.B: It equals N exactly, since Chern–Simons fields affect only Hall response
options.C: It is m*/(8πℏ²), one quarter of N due to Landau quantization
options.D: It diverges at half filling, unlike the finite zero-field N

questions.rationale: The compressibility is three quarters of N and the paper attributes this difference to Chern–Simons interactions.

questions.rationale: Equation 20 gives the established T^(4/3) drag law at half filling.

questions.question: Why can the drag enhancement appear nearly quadratic and symmetric in Δν despite a linear correction?

options.A: The quadratic term scales as T^(2/3) and overtakes the linear contribution, which scales as T^(4/3), at low T
options.B: The linear term cancels exactly between the two identical layers
options.C: The linear term is odd in layer spacing and vanishes at equal spacings
options.D: The experimental observable squares ρD and removes odd powers

questions.rationale: The differing temperature powers make the quadratic correction dominant at low temperatures, reducing asymmetry.
questions.evidence_quote: the second one is proportional to (T/T0)2/3 and predominates at low temperatures

questions.question: Under what condition does the model explain the observed weak sensitivity to interlayer spacing?

options.A: α>1, so T0=(πe²nd/ε)(1+α) becomes nearly independent of d
options.B: α<1, so screening is negligible and T0 scales linearly with d
options.C: α=0, so the interlayer potential cancels from the drag integral
options.D: kFR≫1, so the orbit radius removes all dependence on T0

questions.rationale: Spacing enters through T0, whose dependence on d weakens substantially when α exceeds unity.
questions.evidence_quote: nearly independent of the interlayer separation d when the parameter α takes on values larger that unity

questions.question: What added physical ingredient resolves the RPA estimate's failure to obtain α>1 with the bare GaAs band mass?

options.A: Fermi-liquid renormalization can lower CF compressibility through f0 and thereby raise α
options.B: Finite layer thickness increases the bare CF mass to zero
options.C: Disorder broadening eliminates the interlayer Coulomb potential
options.D: The ballistic approximation changes the sign of the dielectric constant

questions.rationale: The renormalized compressibility dn*/dμ can be substantially reduced, increasing the screening parameter α.
questions.evidence_quote: taking into account Fermi liquid interactions among quasiparticles (CFs)
